dedupe_keys.name: copernicus urban atlas land use street tree layer building height

description: The Urban Atlas provides pan-European comparable land cover and land use maps for Functional Urban Areas (FUA), produced by the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service, whose land activities are delegated by the European Union to the European Environment Agency (EEA) and the Joint Research Centre. The suite covers 788 Functional Urban Areas and includes detailed land use polygons derived from very high resolution imagery, change layers, a separate Street Tree Layer mapping contiguous rows or patches of trees of 500 square metres or more, building block heights for core urban areas and population estimates. Data exist for the 2006, 2012, 2018 and 2021 reference years with change products for 2006-2012, 2012-2018 and 2018-2021; the minimum mapping unit ranges from 0.25 to 1 hectare depending on class, and the update cycle is six years. Products are downloaded as vector datasets from the CLMS portal under the Copernicus data policy of free, full and open access, with attribution to the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service. Caveats: coverage is limited to European urban areas, class definitions changed between reference years, and the street tree layer omits isolated trees. It serves urban green and blue infrastructure inventories, heat and flood exposure analysis, climate adaptation planning and digital twins of cities; related records are the High Resolution Layer Tree Cover and Forests and ESA WorldCover.
